correctness.rationale: Under independent homogeneous q and nonempty latent neighborhoods, proper-subset extinction exponents are exact integer set-union coverages. Write F_N(A)=N−u(P\A), F_N(∅)=0. Möbius inversion yields x_T=b_T+(−1)^{|T|+1}N for every nonempty neighborhood type. Its nonnegativity is equivalent to L≤N≤U, every integer realizes a network with that exact observation law, and fixed N determines the multiset. Even/odd parity neighborhoods anchored at plant m have identical census and every coextinction marginal through order m−2 but differ at order m−1. m=3 gives N=6,7,8. Independently exhaustively tested every incidence vector x_T∈{0,1,2} on m=2,3, including candidate boundaries, not as proof for general m.

value.rationale: PASS: recovering a latent ecological incidence network from missing full-group extinction events is a natural inverse-identifiability question. A sharp complete integer compatibility interval, an explicit construction for every possible census, and matching-census m−2 parity counterexamples determine what observations are indispensable. Classical inclusion–exclusion is a tool, not the result.

limitations: Exact population coextinction probabilities, known q∈(0,1), nonempty pollinator neighborhoods, no feedback or observation noise.
Brute force checks m=2,3 only; universal theorem is Möbius identity.
Marginal polytope and binary OR identifiability literature could formulate the same parity one-dimensional fiber generally.
Exact probabilities and known homogeneous q are strong practical assumptions; finite-sample estimation not addressed.
